He was started on azithromycin once the mycoplasma antibody came positive, which was continued for 5 days.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection presenting with CNS manifestations in the form of stroke and meningoencephalitis, with asymptomatic arterial aneurysms
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 39-year-old man presented with acute-onset fever, headache, neck pain, and lethargy. Neurological examination revealed lethargy, positive neck stiffness, and positive Kernig's sign, suggesting CNS involvement. CSF analysis showed lymphocytic pleocytosis with elevated protein, normal glucose, and negative bacterial/viral tests, consistent with aseptic meningoencephalitis. Brain MRI revealed an acute infarct in the left centrum semi-ovale. Mycoplasma pneumoniae IgM antibody was positive, confirming Mycoplasma infection. A conventional angiogram identified aneurysms in the left subclavian artery and aortic arch. The patient was initially treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics and antivirals, then switched to azithromycin upon Mycoplasma confirmation, and received aspirin for stroke. He became afebrile, headache subsided, and sensorium improved, with complete resolution of neurological deficits after physiotherapy, remaining asymptomatic at 1-month and 3-month follow-up.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with symptoms and signs of CNS involvement, including fever, headache, neck pain, lethargy, positive neck stiffness, and positive Kernig's sign.

CSF analysis showed lymphocytic pleocytosis (58 WBCs, 92% lymphocytes), mild protein elevation (52 mg/dL), normal glucose, and negative Gram stain, culture, and PCR for common viruses, consistent with aseptic meningoencephalitis.
Electroencephalogram showed generalised slowing, further supporting CNS involvement/meningoencephalitis.
Brain MRI showed an acute infarct in the left centrum semi-ovale.
Mycoplasma pneumoniae IgM antibody was positive (titre 1:100), indicating Mycoplasma infection.
Conventional angiogram revealed aneurysms in the left subclavian artery and aortic arch.
Treatment included azithromycin for Mycoplasma infection and aspirin for stroke, leading to clinical improvement.
Patient's neurological deficits completely improved with physiotherapy, and he was asymptomatic at 1-month and 3-month follow-up.
